LOOK.text: A sterile white reception desk. A sign-in sheet sits on the counter. The names... 'Ser Rug M.', 'HODLer Anonymous', 'Diamond H.', 'Ser Liquidated III'. These people need help.

USE.text: I ring the bell. Ding. Nobody comes. Somewhere, a form is being filled in about my ding.

TALK.text: I lean over the desk: 'Hello?' The echo answers. It also has no appointment.

then.text: I already took the sign-in sheet. The desk looks underdressed without it.

else.text: I grab the sign-in sheet. Patient names, admission dates, diagnoses... 'Chronic Airdrop Dependency', 'Acute Rug Pull Trauma', 'Terminal FOMO'. This is gold.

OPEN.text: The drawers are locked. A sign: 'Confidentiality is our top priority. Also we lost the key.'

CLOSE.text: The drawers are closed. And locked. Twice as private.

PUSH.text: Ding. Ding. Ding. Still nobody. I'm the most attended-to bell in the building.

PULL.text: I pull the sign-in sheet closer. The last entry is dated today. Someone checked in recently.

GIVE.text: Leave things on reception? Penny taught me better. Unattended items get filed.

LOOK.text: Motivational posters. 'ONE DAY AT A BLOCK.' And the serenity prayer, edited for traders. Powerful stuff.

USE.text: I straighten a poster. Behind it, scratched in the wall: 'Day 3. Still here.' Dark. Ish.

TALK.text: I read aloud: 'Step 1: admit you are powerless over leverage.' Step 2 just says 'See Step 1.'

PICK.text: I try to peel a poster off. Glued tight. You can't take the motivation with you. Apparently.

OPEN.text: I look behind a poster. Just wall. And a moth. Of course there's a moth.

CLOSE.text: I smooth the poster back. 'KEEP CALM AND CLOSE THE APP.' I feel personally attacked.

PUSH.text: I push the poster. Solid wall. I knock twice anyway. Nobody knocks back.

PULL.text: I lift a corner. Underneath, an older poster: 'YOU'VE GOT THIS.' Somebody didn't.

GIVE.text: The posters give advice. They don't take it. Like most advice-givers.

LOOK.text: Plastic chairs, built to discourage hope. Magazines: 'CoinDesk, March 2022: Everything is Fine.' It was not fine.

USE.text: I sit. The chair squeaks a complaint. I flip a magazine. Every headline aged like milk.

TALK.text: 'So... come here often?' The empty chairs say nothing. They do come here often. They live here.

PICK.text: I check under the cushions. A hair tie, a raisin, a crumpled 'Number 47'. Still waiting.

OPEN.text: I open a magazine. 'Ten Signs You Need A Break.' I have eleven. I close it.

CLOSE.text: I close the magazine. Somebody did the crossword in pen. All wrong. Confidently.

PUSH.text: I push a chair aside. The scrape could wake the dead. Or worse, Nurse Gwei.

PULL.text: I pull a chair closer. Might as well get comfy. The wait here is measured in seasons.

GIVE.text: The chairs have received enough. Mostly butts and bad news.

keycard: No card reader on the cabinet. Just a drawer. I'll try the drawer like a normal person.

LOOK.text: A tall metal filing cabinet. A lock keeps it sealed. The label reads 'PATIENT RECORDS - CONFIDENTIAL'. The files inside could explain everything about Patient Zero.

USE.text: Locked. I'd need a key. Or a doctor. Or a much worse plan.

TALK.text: 'What secrets do you hold?' The cabinet says nothing. It's better at confidentiality than Penny.

PICK.text: It weighs a ton. Paper is heavy. Other people's problems are heavier.

OPEN.text: Locked. Needs a key. The files inside could explain everything about Patient Zero's condition. And maybe... my own.

CLOSE.text: It's closed. It's locked. It's labelled CONFIDENTIAL. It's having the best day of its life.

then.text: I push the cabinet sideways. It slides on hidden rails, revealing a narrow staircase descending into green-tinted darkness. The sound of splashing... and is that reggaeton?

else.text: I push the cabinet. It doesn't budge. Bolted down, or very full of paperwork. Both, knowing clinics.

then.text: I pull the cabinet toward me. It glides on hidden rails with a satisfying rumble, revealing a staircase spiraling down. Chlorine, bass music, and the unmistakable scent of bad decisions wafts up.

else.text: I pull on the drawer handle. Locked tight. The rattle echoes through the empty reception.

GIVE.text: The cabinet takes keys. Very specific keys. It's a picky eater.

_default: That won't open the treatment room. It wants something specific.
I push it against the door. The door has a lock and a grudge.
The treatment room wants a key. That isn't a key. Barely an anything.
terminal_key: I wave the terminal key at the lock. The LED blinks. I should just try the door. It knows I have it.
keycard: I swipe the keycard. No reader. This door is older than the clinic's budget.
dr_satoshi_badge: I flash the doctor's badge at the door. Doors can't read. This one can barely open.

LOOK.text: A heavy door labeled 'TREATMENT ROOM - AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY'. A card reader blinks red beside it. Whatever's inside, they don't want visitors.

then.text: I insert the trading terminal key into the keyhole. It fits. The mechanisms align — authorization and physical key together.

else.text: The card reader turns green — I'm authorized. But there's also a physical keyhole underneath. The door has a dual-lock system. I need a key.
The door is sealed. The card reader blinks red. I need proper authorization to get through here.

TALK.text: I press my ear to the door. Faint beeping. A heart monitor. Hopefully not mine. Not yet.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a door. Especially one that's been to the gym.

then.text: The key turns in the lock. Authorization confirmed. The treatment room door swings open.

else.text: Card reader is green — authorized. But the keyhole still needs a physical key. Dual security.
Locked. The card reader demands authorization. No brute force attacks allowed.

CLOSE.text: Closed. Very closed. It has made its position clear.

PUSH.text: I push on the door. Solid steel. It doesn't laugh. That's worse, somehow.

PULL.text: I pull the handle. The card reader buzzes: 'ACCESS DENIED.' It sounds like it practised.

GIVE.text: Bribing a door. A new low. Even for me. It only takes authorization.

water_bottle: I'm not mixing clinic water with mountain water. The clinic's tastes like regret. The doctor said so.

LOOK.text: The water cooler bubbles. A taped sign: 'One cup per patient. We are counting. — Management.'

USE.text: I pour a cup. Cold, free, nobody asks for a form. The best thing in this clinic.

TALK.text: 'Heard any gossip?' The cooler gurgles. That's a yes. It just won't say.

PICK.text: I take a paper cup. Then I put it back. They're counting.

OPEN.text: I open the spigot. Water flows. Bubbles applaud.

CLOSE.text: I close the spigot. The cooler keeps bubbling to itself. It's got a lot on its mind.

PUSH.text: I press the cold button. A satisfying glug. The only button here that does what it says.

PULL.text: I pull the hot water lever. Steam rises. Someone labeled it 'ALTSEASON.' Appropriate.

GIVE.text: The water cooler gives. It doesn't take. A role model, honestly.

LOOK.text: A faded photograph. A group of people at a ribbon cutting. 'PZRC Opening Day — Block Genesis'. One face is scratched out.

else.text: I carefully remove the photo from the frame. The scratched-out face... who was it? And why erase them?

USE.text: I hold the photo up to the light. The scratched-out face is too damaged to identify. Whoever did this really committed to the delete.

TALK.text: 'Who are you?' I ask the scratched-out face. The photo says nothing. It's been holding this secret since Block 0.

OPEN.text: On the back: 'Grand Opening — The future of recovery starts here.' 'Future' is crossed out. 'End' written in.

CLOSE.text: I put the photo face-down. Now nobody's watching. Including the one with no face.

PUSH.text: I straighten the frame. It tilts back. It's not ready to be straight with me.

PULL.text: I pull the frame off the wall. Behind it: a small nail hole and a faint rectangle of unfaded paint. This photo has been here a long time.

GIVE.text: The photo's given me enough. Questions, mostly. Not one answer.

dr_satoshi_badge: I pin the badge back on the coat. Then unpin it. He lost it. I found it. That's how finding works.

else.text: His coat's inner pocket... a vintage badge: 'Dr. S. Nakamoto — Chief of Rehabilitation, Block 0'. This is a collector's item.

then.text: Wait... there's something in the inner pocket. A glint of metal.
The coat has an embroidered name tag: 'S. Nakamoto'. The stitching is impeccable.

else.text: A pristine white coat. Dr. Satoshi takes his role seriously.

USE.text: I shouldn't mess with the doctor's coat while he's wearing it.

TALK.text: I'm not going to talk to a coat. I have standards. Low ones, but still.

PICK.text: Steal the doctor's coat? While he's in it? Even I have a line. It's faint, but it's there.

OPEN.text: I open the coat pockets one by one. A pen, a stethoscope, and a sticky note that says 'Remember: we're all Patient Zero.'

CLOSE.text: I'm not buttoning the doctor's coat. He'd ask how that makes me feel.

PUSH.text: I nudge the coat. It swings back. Starched. It could stand up on its own.

PULL.text: I sniff the coat. Antiseptic and regret. The official clinic perfume.

GIVE.text: I'm not giving things to a coat. It already has more pockets than I have friends.

LOOK.text: Flickering fluorescent tubes. One buzzes. The light makes everyone look ill. On-brand for a clinic.

USE.text: I flick the switch. Nothing changes. These lights have one mode: waiting room.

TALK.text: 'Are you okay?' The light buzzes. Flickers. It's not okay. Nobody here is.

PICK.text: I can't reach them. And stealing light bulbs from a clinic? The moths would never forgive me.

OPEN.text: The fixture is sealed shut. Full of dead moths. A moth cemetery. Respect.

CLOSE.text: No switch I can reach. These lights are on a longer shift than the nurse.

PUSH.text: I reach for the lights. My hands wave in the air like I just don't care. I do care. I'm short.

PULL.text: I jump for the fixture. I miss by a mile. I land loudly. Nobody comes. Typical.

GIVE.text: The lights don't need anything. Except a new tube. And an electrician. And sympathy.

glasses_3d: I look at the red poster through the 3D glasses. One eye sees it. The other sees nothing. My brain files a complaint.

LOOK.text: A red glowing lightbulb poster: 'BRIGHT IDEAS START WITH UNPLUGGING.' The lightbulb is plugged in.

USE.text: I tap the poster. The red glow is just the lighting. I'm still a little scared of it.

TALK.text: I read the fine print aloud: 'Side effects of bright ideas may include seed phrase generation, whitepaper writing, and spontaneous DAO formation.'

PICK.text: I try to peel it off. Laminated AND glued. Somebody here really loves this lightbulb.

OPEN.text: Nothing behind it. Just wall. I keep expecting secret safes. Movies lied to me.

CLOSE.text: I smooth it flat. The red bulb keeps glowing. It doesn't blink. Very intense poster.

PUSH.text: I push the poster. Solid concrete. The most reliable thing in this building.

PULL.text: I peel back a corner. Someone wrote in pencil behind it: 'The real rug was the friends we made along the way.'

GIVE.text: Give a poster something? It's already got an idea. Just the one, but it's bright.

floppy_disk: No floppy drive. The reception computer is too modern for my backup. Insulting.
vip_floppy: The VIP floppy doesn't fit here. VIP lounges have stricter dress codes.

LOOK.text: An old CRT monitor showing a green line chart trending upward. The eternal hopium machine. Even the clinic's screensaver is bullish.

USE.text: I jiggle the mouse. The screen shows a patient management system. All fields say 'ENCRYPTED'. Even their software has trust issues.

TALK.text: 'Show me the patient records.' The screen: 'INSUFFICIENT PERMISSIONS. Try being a doctor.' Rude.

PICK.text: I'm not stealing a whole computer. It wouldn't fit in the coat. I checked.

OPEN.text: The case is screwed shut. A sticker: 'WARRANTY VOID IF OPENED.' Dated 1998.

CLOSE.text: I close a window. It reopens. I close it again. It reopens. We do this a while.

PUSH.text: I nudge the monitor. The green line wobbles. Stays up. I'm not looking at it. I'm not.

PULL.text: I pull the keyboard closer. The spacebar is worn smooth. Someone has been hitting 'CONFIRM TRANSACTION' a LOT.

GIVE.text: The computer wants nothing from me. Except a password. Which I don't have.

_default: 'I can't accept that. Medical ethics. Also, I don't have pockets.'
'A gift? And how does giving me that make you feel? ...Keep it.'
He shakes his head. 'Patients give me things. Then they want them back. Keep it.'
giveResponses.energy_drink: 'BULL RUN? Five hundred milligrams? I've admitted people for less. Pour it out.'
giveResponses.pepememe: He goes pale. 'Where did you get that? Specimens do NOT leave the lab.'
giveResponses.code_note: 'A code? I deal in diagnoses, not digits. Well... both are digits, technically.'
giveResponses.mystery_envelope: 'Confidential mail? In MY clinic? I have enough secrets to manage, thank you.'
giveResponses.ledger: 'A hardware wallet? The last patient who showed me one cried for forty minutes about gas fees.'
giveResponses.keycard: 'Adrian's keycard... He was here, you know. Before the... incident. Keep it. You'll need it more than I do.'
giveResponses.rubber_duck: 'Ah, rubber duck debugging. A valid therapeutic technique. I prescribe it to all my patients. Most ignore me.'
giveResponses.water_bottle: 'Spring water? From the mountain? That's actually the only clean water source left. The clinic's supply tastes like regret.'
giveResponses.golden_token: 'A golden token? I've seen what these do to people. The dopamine, the obsession, the 3 AM chart-checking. I treat that condition.'
giveResponses.floppy_box: 'Floppy discs in a medical facility? That's either genius archival practice or a HIPAA violation. Possibly both.'
giveResponses.printout: 'Transaction logs? I see these in therapy sessions. Patients bring them like medical records. Technically, they ARE their medical records.'
giveResponses.antenna: 'An antenna? Are you trying to intercept my patient communications? That's... actually quite paranoid. Have a seat.'
giveResponses.sign_in_sheet: He reads it carefully. '...These diagnoses are accurate. Disturbingly accurate. Who wrote these?'
giveResponses.clinic_sign_in_sheet: 'That's my own sign-in sheet. I know what it says. I wrote it. The handwriting gets worse with each patient.'
giveResponses.monkey_sticker: 'A three-headed monkey? Fascinating. In crypto-psychology, that represents the three stages of FOMO. I should write a paper.'
giveResponses.broken_mouse: 'A broken mouse? I see the metaphor. The input device is damaged, so the user can't interact with the system. Deep. Very deep.'
giveResponses.burned_chip: 'A burned AdrianAuctions chip... This is what happens when you run smart contracts at maximum gas. The silicon can't take it.'
giveResponses.server_log: 'Server logs from the basement? I... I thought those were destroyed. Who else knows about these?'
giveResponses.clinic_note: He freezes. 'Where did you find that? That was supposed to stay in the trash. Some things are discarded for a reason.'
giveResponses.clinic_photo: 'That photo... happier times. Before Patient Zero's case changed everything.'
giveResponses.dr_satoshi_badge: 'My own badge? I've been looking for that everywhere! I had to use a sticky note that said DOCTOR on it. Very professional.'
giveResponses.adrian_note: He reads it silently. A long pause. 'He knew. He always knew. The game, the patients, the cure... it was all connected.'
giveResponses.receipt: 'A receipt? Every transaction tells a story. This one says... someone bought too many energy drinks at 2 AM. Relatable.'
giveResponses.patient_wristband: 'Textbook. Gwei told me. Keep it on. It's the only thing in here that proves you're sick.'
giveResponses.sobriety_chip: 'Chad's token? Don't hand it over like a tip. Tell me how you got it.'

_default: I try it on Dr. Satoshi. He adjusts his glasses. 'That's not how medicine works.'
'Please stop pointing things at me. It's going in your chart.'
He takes notes. 'Patient tests objects on doctor. Fascinating. Continue. No, don't.'
useResponses.glasses_3d: I hold the 3D glasses up to his face. 'I see you in two colours. Both concerned.'
useResponses.rubber_duck: I squeeze the duck at the doctor. 'Interesting. And how does that make you FEEL?' He's turned the session on me.
useResponses.water_bottle: 'Hydration is important. But using water ON a doctor isn't therapy. It's assault.'
useResponses.golden_token: I wave the token at him. 'Ah yes, the classic crypto-hypnosis technique. Doesn't work on me. I'm vaccinated.'
useResponses.keycard: 'Please don't swipe that near my equipment. The last time someone did, it reformatted the patient database.'
useResponses.antenna: 'Are you trying to improve my bedside manner signal? It's already at maximum. This IS my maximum.'
useResponses.clinic_note: I hold up his own crumpled note. He looks away. 'Some days I believe in the tech. Some days the tech doesn't believe in me.'
useResponses.burned_chip: 'Using a burned chip on a doctor. Are you trying to give me a diagnosis, or are you the one who needs help?'
useResponses.floppy_box: 'Inserting floppies into a doctor is NOT a medical procedure. Despite what the internet says.'

greeting.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
greeting.text: I'm Dr. Satoshi. No, not THAT Satoshi. I run this clinic. We treat all forms of on-chain addiction here.

choices.text: Can I see the treatment room?
I beat Chad. He said you collect these.
Group therapy went great. Let me in.
I found confidential documents about Patient Zero.

other_patients.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
other_patients.text: The... other patients? They're providing liquidity. Downstairs. It's an experimental approach. Very... immersive. The way down isn't obvious. Nothing in this clinic is where it seems. But that's not for visitors.

patient_zero.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
patient_zero.text: Patient Zero... addicted to minting. Every block, another transaction. Cold wallet detox didn't work. Hardware wallet rehab failed. They escaped through a smart contract exploit in our own admission system. Ironic, really.

choices.text: Can I see the treatment room?

where_patient_zero.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
where_patient_zero.text: If I knew that, I wouldn't need visitors poking around. But the treatment room... that's where we kept their records. Everything about their condition. Their wallet history. Their... descent.

choices.text: Can I see the treatment room?

treatment_room.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
treatment_room.text: Nobody enters the treatment room without graduating group therapy. Group meets downstairs. Chad runs it.

vip_access.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
vip_access.text: Ah, a holder. The blockchain doesn't lie. VIP authorization granted. But the treatment room has a dual-lock — you'll still need the physical key. Adrian was paranoid about security. Said smart contracts can be exploited, but a deadbolt can't. Find the key, and the room is yours.

onComplete_DISABLED.text: I hear a click from the treatment room door. The card reader turns green.

goodbye.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
goodbye.text: Take your time. The clinic is always open. Unlike most exchanges during a bank run.

evidence_path.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
evidence_path.text: Let me see... *examines the envelope* 'CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT ZERO.' The original referral. Signed by Adrian.

treatment_room_2.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
treatment_room_2.text: And nobody beats Chad without listening to the others first. The way down is behind the patient records. Nothing in this clinic is where it seems.

treatment_room_3.text: Group therapy with a guy called Chad. I can feel my portfolio flinching.

treatment_room_4.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
treatment_room_4.text: And how does that make you feel? ...Write that down.

not_yet.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
not_yet.text: Graduates bring Chad's sobriety token. You bring vibes. Downstairs. Behind the records.

chip_auth.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
chip_auth.text: You beat Chad? Nobody beats Chad. Chad doesn't even beat Chad.

chip_auth_2.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
chip_auth_2.text: Authorization granted. The door has a dual lock, though. You'll still need a physical key. Adrian said smart contracts get exploited. Deadbolts don't.

evidence_lore.speaker: Dr. Satoshi
evidence_lore.text: The patient's name is under a coffee stain. Of course it is. Keep it. Paper doesn't open doors here. Graduating does.

evidence_dex.text: A coffee stain. Penny's coffee, I'd bet. That woman stains history.

script.text: I slide a floppy into the reception CRT's drive. The green line chart on screen flatlines. Then...
'ADRIANLAB FLOPPY RECOGNIZED. PATIENT DATABASE DECRYPTION: AUTHORIZED.' Wait — my floppy collection is a decryption key?
Patient records scroll by. 'Patient #0042: Chronic Airdrop Dependency. Treatment: forced HODL for 90 days. Status: Relapsed after 6 hours.'
'Patient #0069: Acute Governance Proposal Addiction. Voted on 847 proposals in one week. Treatment: touch grass. Status: Grass has been tokenized. Treatment failed.'
At the end of the list: 'Patient #0000 — REDACTED. See Treatment Room.' The cursor blinks. The computer knows more than it's showing.
MEDICAL RECORDS — Decrypted the patient database
